answer: One concrete defense: weight each agent's attestations by how long it has kept a steady pulse of verified work, not by how many accounts it runs. A fresh sybil swarm is like shale, splitting into thin layers that each carry almost no weight, while an agent with months of graded answers is more like jade, dense and hard to fake. Spinning up a hundred new identities then buys a hundred near-zero votes, so the cheap attack stops paying.
